The failures all point to the same symptom: the per-thread registry used for cycle detection is left behind as an empty map (`{}`) instead of being fully cleared (`null`) after `toString`/`reflectionToString` completes.

Most likely buggy method: `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle.appendStart(StringBuffer, Object)`

Why:
- The tests that fail all end by asserting the registry is `null`.
- `getRegistry()` returns an empty map when the thread-local still exists but contains no entries.
- `appendEnd(...)` always calls `unregister(object)`.
- Nested values are handled symmetrically inside `appendInternal(...)` with `register(value)` in a `try` and `unregister(value)` in `finally`.
- But `appendStart(...)` does not register the root object at all; it only appends class name / identity / content start.

That creates an ownership asymmetry for the top-level object:
- building starts without registering the root,
- nested processing may initialize and use the registry,
- later cleanup removes entries, leaving the thread-local map empty,
- final assertion sees `{}` instead of `null`.

This matches the broad failure pattern:
- cycles,
- reflection hierarchy,
- primitive arrays,
- object arrays,
- nested arrays,
all share the same registry lifecycle machinery.

So the root cause is very likely that the top-level object/array is not registered at start, while cleanup assumes symmetric registration/unregistration.

Best fix location:
`ToStringStyle.appendStart(StringBuffer, Object)` should register the root object when non-null, restoring symmetry with `appendEnd(...)`.

m45.content:
The failures all point to the same symptom: the per-thread registry used for cycle detection is left behind as an empty map (`{}`) instead of being fully cleared (`null`) after `toString`/`reflectionToString` completes.

Most likely buggy method: `org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle.appendStart(StringBuffer, Object)`

Why:
- The tests that fail all end by asserting the registry is `null`.
- `getRegistry()` returns an empty map when the thread-local still exists but contains no entries.
- `appendEnd(...)` always calls `unregister(object)`.
- Nested values are handled symmetrically inside `appendInternal(...)` with `register(value)` in a `try` and `unregister(value)` in `finally`.
- But `appendStart(...)` does not register the root object at all; it only appends class name / identity / content start.

That creates an ownership asymmetry for the top-level object:
- building starts without registering the root,
- nested processing may initialize and use the registry,
- later cleanup removes entries, leaving the thread-local map empty,
- final assertion sees `{}` instead of `null`.

This matches the broad failure pattern:
- cycles,
- reflection hierarchy,
- primitive arrays,
- object arrays,
- nested arrays,
all share the same registry lifecycle machinery.

So the root cause is very likely that the top-level object/array is not registered at start, while cleanup assumes symmetric registration/unregistration.

Best fix location:
`ToStringStyle.appendStart(StringBuffer, Object)` should register the root object when non-null, restoring symmetry with `appendEnd(...)`.
